title: Dedicated autoscaler: priority fallback for burst controls + utilization reporting enhancement
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: In heavy burst scenarios some lower-priority tenants were experiencing long queueing delays or sudden throughput drops when higher-priority traffic consumed burst tokens. This PR implements a priority-aware fallback policy for burst controls and improves fleet utilization reporting so SRE and product teams can observe per-priority headroom and make capacity decisions. Summary of changes: 1) Autoscaler: add PriorityFallbackPolicy which dynamically relaxes burst caps for mid-priority queues when system-wide headroom exists and temporarily throttles non-critical low-priority traffic. This uses a short window (configurable) to avoid oscillation. 2) Token-bucket smoothing: tune smoothing constants and expose diagnostics for token refill rates per-priority. 3) Utilization reporting: emit new metrics (dedicated.fleet.burst_headroom_bytes, dedicated.fleet.priority_utilization_percent, dedicated.fleet.fallback_actions_total) and aggregate labels (fleet_id, priority_level). 4) Observability: add Grafana dashboard changes and a tracing span for fallback decisions. 5) Tests: unit tests for policy selector, integration tests simulating multi-tenant bursts, and an e2e canary with a synthetic workload. Rollout plan: behind feature flag dedicated.autoscaler.priority_fallback; canary on 5% of fleets for 48 hours, monitor latency and queueing SLOs; if regressions <1% and no errors, graduate to 100% over 6 hours. Linked work: ENG-4382 (priority autoscaling), ENG-4405 (util reporting), SUP-2148 (customer incident root cause). Checklist: - [x] Implementation of PriorityFallbackPolicy and config schema - [x] Unit tests and integration tests - [x] Metrics and dashboard updates - [x] Documentation: docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md updated with behavior and flags - [x] Feature flag gating and rollout doc - [x] Performance run against perf-canary infra - [x] Changelog/release note added
